title: Replicating SAE Feature Visualization Across ViT Scales: Does Feature Polysemanticity Increase in Larger CLIP Models?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Whether larger vision models are more or less polysemantic informs whether scaling naturally improves interpretability. This is relevant to the broader scaling debate in AI safety but the impact chain to a concrete safety intervention is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prisma provides pre-trained SAEs for all three CLIP ViT sizes. No training needed, just inference and feature analysis. Medium compute is sufficient for CLIP ViT inference. Automated interpretability scoring is the main technical challenge but methods exist.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-defined comparison: monosemanticity fraction across three model sizes at matched relative depths. Single metric, single model family, pre-trained SAEs available. Clean deliverable as a scaling curve. Achievable in 30 hours.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
